components.name: Primary Button

components.name: Outline Button

narrative.overview:
This is a space designed for people on the edge of a decision — curious, perhaps nervous, but ready to commit. The visual system is built around two ideas held in tension: Trevor's authority as an expert, and genuine accessibility for a first-time client. Heavyweight Oswald type at large scales communicates that he knows exactly what he is doing. Deliberate negative space and a near-black palette communicate that this is premium, not overwhelming.

The site is dark because its audience encounters it as a considered choice — usually at home, researching trainers, in a quiet moment of self-motivation. The darkness is not gym-chain aggression; it is focused calm. One flame-colored accent (Ignition Orange) marks every point of action and creates visual momentum without saturation overload.

This system explicitly rejects generic gym-chain aesthetics, corporate wellness sterility, and the hustle-funnel approach. The emotional arc of every page is: intrigue, then credibility, then inspiration, then contact — never urgency before trust.
keyCharacteristics: Two-weight type scale: massive Oswald display vs. restrained Archivo body
One primary accent, used sparingly and treated as directional signal
Tonal dark layering from near-black to charcoal
Bold structural shadows that carve surfaces on hover
Scroll-triggered stagger entrances — no gratuitous choreography

rules.name: The One Flame Rule
rules.body: Ignition Orange appears on no more than 15% of any given screen. Its scarcity is the signal.

rules.name: The Warm-Only Rule
rules.body: Both accents are warm-spectrum. Never introduce cool accents (blue, teal, purple).

rules.name: The Oswald-Uppercase Contract
rules.body: Oswald at Display and Headline scales is always uppercase. Mixed-case Oswald at large scales loses its authority.

rules.name: The Scale Ratio Rule
rules.body: Maintain a minimum 1.25x contrast ratio between adjacent hierarchy steps.

rules.name: The Active Surface Rule
rules.body: Shadows deepen in response to interaction, never at rest as decoration alone.

dos: Do use Oswald uppercase at Display and Headline scales.
Do reserve Ignition Orange for CTAs, check-icons, and hierarchy markers — one dominant use per viewport section.
Do apply structural shadows that deepen on hover: Surface at rest, Raised on interaction.
Do vary section vertical padding for rhythm: py-20 for informational sections, py-32 for statement sections.
Do animate scroll entrances with whileInView + staggerChildren for grid sections.
Do ensure warm-accent elements hold WCAG AA contrast against their backgrounds.
donts: Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient). Use solid orange or white with weight/size for emphasis.
Don't build generic gym-chain aesthetics: primary red/blue/yellow palettes, stock-photo muscle imagery.
Don't use corporate wellness styling: white-dominant layouts, sterile card grids, clinical spacing.
Don't build hustle-funnel patterns: countdown timers, stacked testimonial walls, repeated aggressive CTAs.
Don't use border-left greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards or list items.
Don't extend the nav backdrop-blur to cards or section dividers — it is structural and specific.
Don't place a CTA before credibility is established in the page flow.
Don't use Drive Red on primary CTAs.
